title: free2z store identity
description: The non-secret facts about cash.free2z.free2z's two store records that the release path must bind to but cannot discover. Every field that is null names something a human must create in App Store Connect or Google Play Console first; the release path refuses to sign or upload while any field it needs is still null, and says which one.

distributionIdentity.description: The codesigning identity the shared Corpora Apple Distribution certificate presents. Team-wide, not app-specific: this is the certificate ZUULI and e2e2z already sign with.

appStoreConnectRecord.description: Whether an App Store Connect app record exists for this bundle id. It cannot be created from the API; a human creates it in App Store Connect. For cash.free2z.free2z it already exists (app name "Free2Z", SKU cash.free2z.free2z).

provisioningProfileName.description: The App Store distribution provisioning profile's name, exactly as it appears in ExportOptions.plist. A profile named `free2z appstore ci` has been issued for this bundle id (application-identifier F9AV5HKF6N.cash.free2z.free2z, associated-domains present, expiring 2027-08-08) but is not yet installed as a repository secret, and its UUID has not been read out of the file, so this stays null until both are recorded together.

provisioningProfileUuid.description: The same profile's UUID, used to place and then prove the removal of the ephemeral profile on the signing runner. Read it with `security cms -D -i <profile>.mobileprovision | plutil -extract UUID raw -o - -`.

playConsoleListing.description: Whether a Play Console listing exists for this package name. The Android Publisher API can only edit an app that already exists; a human creates it in Play Console.

uploadCertificateSha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the upload certificate whose private key signs the AAB, uppercase and colon-delimited, exactly as `keytool -list -v` prints it. Null until an upload key exists and Play Console has accepted it.

appSigningCertificateSha256.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate Play App Signing re-signs with, which is what assetlinks.json must carry. Play generates it: it is readable only from Play Console (Setup -> App integrity -> App signing) after the listing exists. It is recorded here for the assetlinks work; the release path itself never uses it.
